why_ai: Inspectors walk, drive and listen to every car on the lot and lot drivers move it, while bidding and settlement have moved online; the middleman role survives because physical cars still need grading and moving.
why_clarity: Each car sells or no-sells within minutes and arbitration grades the report within days, across millions of near-identical transactions, though the inspector's read is learned by feel.
why_digital: Physical vehicles on lots are graded by hand and delivered by truck, but dealers bid remotely from anywhere and half of in-lane sales go online.

why_ai: Channel, timing and floor decisions are screen work models can take over, but captives place volume with account teams they trust.
why_clarity: Net proceeds against MMR is an exact, agreed measure reported on every unit within weeks, though channel strategy is argued by experience.
why_digital: Unit data, private-label sites and dashboards are digital; the cars still sit on lots and some sell in physical lanes.

why_ai: Lane placement, floor advice and bidder matching are routine predictions on rich data; local dealer relationships give some protection.
why_clarity: Sold or not sold on first run is known at the fall of the hammer, on thousands of runs a week.
why_digital: Run lists, bidding and notifications are online; the consigned car is a physical unit on the auction's lot.

why_ai: Case assembly and threshold checks automate well, but borderline defect calls, post-sale inspections and angry buyers still need a person.
why_clarity: The NAAA guidelines codify thresholds and windows, and each claim ends in an adjustment, unwind or denial within days, though fairness is argued.
why_digital: Claims and evidence arrive digitally, but post-sale inspections and unwinds move physical cars.

why_ai: Tracking titles and funds is rule-bound back-office work that software and agents can carry; state offices and lenders set the pace.
why_clarity: A title is negotiable or not and a payment clears or not, on every sale, checked within days.
why_digital: Funds are electronic, but many titles are still paper documents moved by mail.

why_ai: Chasing documents against a deadline is the kind of follow-up LLM agents now do; no licence or relationship protects it.
why_clarity: Each title arrives inside the window or the sale can be cancelled, a binary outcome on every title-absent unit.
why_digital: Paper titles move physically between sellers, lienholders and states; the tracking and messaging are digital.

why_ai: Credit exposure checks and payment scoring are screen work, though lenders carry accountability for credit lines.
why_clarity: Payments clear or bounce and write-offs are counted exactly, within days of each sale.
why_digital: Floorplan draws, ACH and lender APIs are fully electronic; dealers are served remotely.

why_ai: Serving a family-owned auction means local relationships, an auctioneer in the lane and a lot of physical cars, with tooling bought from a few vendors.
why_clarity: Sale-day conversion and bidder counts are measured each week, though how an independent keeps its dealers varies by owner.
why_digital: Local dealers, physical lanes and check-in by hand, with simulcast and listing networks layered on top.

why_ai: Battery grading needs hands-on scans of physical cars and judgement where data is thin; demand grows as EV returns rise.
why_clarity: There is no agreed battery grade yet, methods differ by make, and whether a grade was right shows only months later.
why_digital: The battery is read from a physical car, but the grade and the sale are digital and buyers bid remotely.

why_ai: Checking announcements against a codified rulebook, a VIN decode and recall data is exactly the mechanical work automation replaces.
why_clarity: The 2026 guidelines spell out prohibited wording and thresholds, and claims later show whether each check was right.
why_digital: Announcements, condition reports, VIN decodes and recall data are all digital inputs and outputs.

why_ai: Cars are physically released at a gate and hauled by drivers, though matching, vetting and photo comparison are automatable.
why_clarity: Each delivery arrives with or without a claim, on the same procedure every time, known within days.
why_digital: Loads are booked online, but the product is a car moved by truck to a dealer's lot.

why_ai: Committing a captive's residual risk is high-stakes judgement, but the forecasting and channel analysis are model work.
why_clarity: Sale results grade channel decisions within weeks, but residual forecasts resolve over the lease term.
why_digital: Lease, condition and sale data analysed on screens; decisions go to auctions and platforms electronically.

why_ai: Programme analytics on a SaaS platform is screen work; the platform's relationships with captives are its protection.
why_clarity: Programme results are measured monthly against floors and MMR, though advice differs by consultant.
why_digital: Platform data in, digital reports and recommendations out, to remote clients.

why_ai: Pricing return and assurance risk from claim history is actuarial modelling that AI accelerates.
why_clarity: Each guaranteed sale is returned or not and each assurance claim paid or not, across thousands of policies.
why_digital: Claims, returns and pricing are data work delivered as terms on a digital sale.

why_ai: The index's authority comes from the publisher's transaction record and benchmark status, which outlasts any model.
why_clarity: A codified, adjusted index recurs monthly and is checked against the next month's transactions.
why_digital: Transaction data in, a published digital index and commentary out.

why_ai: Credit officers sign off on dealer lines and the relationship matters, but the analysis itself is screen work.
why_clarity: Credit policy and curtailment schedules are codified, and payoffs and defaults show within months.
why_digital: Unit-level floorplan data analysed on screens; dealers served remotely with some field audits.

why_ai: Scanners need hardware on site and imaging teams judge what counts as damage, but the models are software that auctions and competitors can build in-house, as ACV did with Monk.
why_clarity: Detected damage is checked against inspectors, buyers and claims on every scan, across hundreds of thousands of vehicles.
why_digital: Images of physical cars in, digital reports out, sold to remote enterprise buyers.

why_ai: Load matching and pricing are platform software; network effects are the protection, not people.
why_clarity: Loads are booked, picked up and delivered or not, thousands of times a day.
why_digital: A fully online marketplace for a physical service delivered by carriers.

why_ai: Title and lien processing is rule-bound transaction work that automates directly.
why_clarity: Each title is perfected, released or transferred correctly or not, by statute.
why_digital: State ELT messages and title images in, digital status out, with some paper still handled.

why_ai: Auction software and a sale-data feed that AI-native competitors can rebuild; switching costs protect it.
why_clarity: Features work on sale day or they do not, across hundreds of client auctions.
why_digital: Software and data built and sold entirely online.

why_ai: Licence and identity verification is routine and automatable; acceptance across 400+ marketplaces is the moat.
why_clarity: A dealer is credentialed or not against a clear rule, instantly checkable.
why_digital: Applications, verification and credentials are fully digital.

why_ai: The association's standing as the industry's rule-writer is what members pay for; drafting and surveys are automatable.
why_clarity: Guidelines are written by committee and their effect on claims shows only over seasons.
why_digital: Surveys, guidelines and training are documents and online material.

why_ai: Acquisitions and regional consignor deals rest on owner relationships and negotiated judgement.
why_clarity: Deals and alliances are one-off and their success shows over years.
why_digital: Group sale data is digital, but the business is physical sites and local relationships.

why_ai: Inspectors must walk each returned car at the lessee's home or a dealer, though camera inspection is eroding the report.
why_clarity: Standardised wear-and-use grades on every return, later disputed or accepted.
why_digital: Starts from a physical car at an address and ends as a digital report sent to a remote lessor.

why_ai: Battery grading needs a device on the car, and demand grows with EV returns, but the analysis is model work.
why_clarity: Grades are numeric and repeatable, but whether they predicted a battery's life shows only years later.
why_digital: Readings from physical cars, reports delivered digitally to remote buyers.

why_ai: Licensing decisions and fraud investigations must be made by accountable officials, sometimes on site.
why_clarity: Statutes frame licensing and disclosure, but investigations are case by case and slow to resolve.
why_digital: Licence files are increasingly online, but audits and investigations happen in person.

why_ai: Trade journalism and events depend on sources and standing; news writing itself is increasingly automatable.
why_clarity: What makes a good story or conference is a matter of taste, with no checkable outcome.
why_digital: Reporting and publishing are online; events are in person.
